module_title: Angle of Contact, Detergents, and Terminal Velocity
introduction: This advanced level explores the mathematical thresholds of fluid behavior, the specific interaction of different liquids with solid surfaces, and the physics of falling through the air.

core_concepts.title: Angle of Contact
core_concepts.description:
The angle formed between the tangent to the liquid surface and the solid surface inside the liquid. 
1. Water & Glass: Adhesive force > Cohesive force. Angle is 'Acute' ($<90^\circ$). Water 'wets' the glass. Meniscus is concave. 
2. Mercury & Glass: Cohesive force > Adhesive force. Angle is 'Obtuse' ($>90^\circ$). Mercury does 'not wet' the glass. Meniscus is convex.

core_concepts.title: Action of Detergents and Soaps
core_concepts.description: Pure water has high surface tension, meaning it doesn't enter the tiny pores of clothes easily. Adding detergent drastically 'lowers the surface tension' and reduces the angle of contact, allowing the water to penetrate fibers and remove dirt.

core_concepts.title: Terminal Velocity
core_concepts.description: When a body falls through a viscous fluid (like a raindrop falling through air), it initially accelerates. However, viscous drag opposes it. Eventually, the downward weight is exactly balanced by the upward drag. The body stops accelerating and falls with a constant, maximum speed called 'Terminal Velocity'.

core_concepts.title: Stokes' Law
core_concepts.description:
It gives the formula for the viscous drag force ($F$) on a small sphere falling through a fluid. 
$F = 6 \pi \eta r v$ 
Where $\eta$ is the coefficient of viscosity, $r$ is the radius, and $v$ is the velocity. This explains why parachutes work.

important_entities.name: Capillary Depression of Mercury
important_entities.significance: Because its cohesive force is massive (forming an obtuse angle), if you dip a capillary tube into a pool of mercury, the level of mercury inside the tube will actually fall 'below' the outside level.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a raindrop fell continuously with the acceleration of gravity ($9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$) from 2 km high, it would hit us like a bullet. It doesn't, because of 'Terminal Velocity' caused by the air's viscosity, which limits its final speed to a safe level.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Water loves glass (Adhesive wins). Mercury loves itself (Cohesive wins).

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS Mains/UPSC Prelims often ask about the shape of the meniscus. Remember: Water in glass = Concave (dips down). Mercury in glass = Convex (bulges up).
